items.title: Kilby Block Party 2027 Lineup Revealed with Deftones, The Strokes & Fontaines D.C.
items.summary:
Kilby Block Party has announced the lineup for its 2027 edition, with Deftones, The Strokes, Fontaines D.C., Slayyyter, Jungle and IDLES heading the bill at the Salt Lake City festival.

The rest of the card leans heavily on the indie rock audience the festival has built around, including Spoon, Kim Gordon, Wednesday, Julien Baker, Atlas Sound, Wolf Parade, Iceage, Weyes Blood, Hot Chip, Phantogram, Kurt Vile and the Violators, Silversun Pickups, Joyce Manor, Two Door Cinema Club, Twin Peaks, Mercury Rev, Ratboys, Lip Critic and Westside Cowboy. Lil Yachty is among the few names working well outside that lane.

The festival runs May 14th through 16th at the Utah State Fairpark, as Consequence reported. Three-day passes start at $245.

A pre-sale opens Wednesday, October 28th at 12 p.m. MT for registered buyers, with the general on-sale following Thursday, October 29th at 10 a.m. PT through the festival's website.

items.title: Palm Springs Kicks Off Honoree Run With ‘The Invite’ Receiving Its Vanguard Award
items.summary:
The Palm Springs International Film Awards will give its Vanguard Award to A24's The Invite, the first honoree announced ahead of the 2027 Palm Springs International Film Festival. The award will be presented at the festival's opening-night gala on January 7.

Director and star Olivia Wilde is expected to attend alongside co-stars Seth Rogen, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton. The Vanguard Award recognizes the combined work of a director and cast, and past recipients include Hamnet last year, as well as Green Book and The Shape of Water, both of which went on to win Best Picture.

The film follows a dinner party between two neighboring couples that turns into an evening of revelations and desire, mining marriage and intimacy for both comedy and discomfort. It opened in theaters in late June and became one of the year's strongest limited debuts, grossing $61.2 million domestically and internationally.

Festival chairman Nachhattar Singh Chandi praised the ensemble in announcing the honor. "With The Invite, Olivia Wilde has made a film that is both comedic and deeply human," he said, adding that the cast "created something that has stayed with audiences long after the credits roll."

Deadline reported the announcement. The Invite premiered at Sundance earlier this year and this week picked up four Gotham Film Awards nominations, tying for the most of any film, including a nod for Will McCormack and Rashida Jones' adapted screenplay. More Palm Springs honorees will be announced in the run-up to the January gala.

items.title: Massive Attack’s Robert Del Naja Releases New Songs for Gaza Documentary
items.summary:
Robert Del Naja of Massive Attack has contributed new music to the soundtrack for Life Support, a documentary about healthcare workers in Gaza. The album arrived today and includes three original tracks credited to Del Naja's 3D alias, plus his remix of Kneecap's "Palestine," featuring Fawzi.

Del Naja curated the record with the film's producers. A fourth contribution comes from the Five Techniques collective on "Resistance in the Dark," which features Paul Weller, David Holmes and Róisín El Cherif. Yasmine Hamdan, Habib Shehada Hanna, Massar Egbari, 47Soul, Aar Maanta, and Siba and Monkyman round out the thirteen-track sequence.

All profits from vinyl sales will go to the Health Workers 4 Palestine solidarity fund, according to a press release cited by Pitchfork.

The film is built from testimonies and footage gathered by international doctors permitted to enter Gaza. Its synopsis describes accounts covering "the entire two years of the genocide," documenting workers moving through "bombed-out hospitals, dwindling supplies, starvation and the overwhelming influx of casualties—predominantly women and children."

Life Support is now streaming on demand, with dozens of screenings scheduled, most of them in the United Kingdom and Ireland, and several paired with filmmaker Q&As. Del Naja was among hundreds of people arrested in London in April for holding placards supporting Palestine Action, a group banned under UK terrorism law.
